title: Graceful degradation simulation: inflight-request quarantine for multi-region partition and GPU pool exhaustion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reproducible chaos-testing harness and runbook that validates graceful degradation when (1) a region is partitioned from control plane and/or other regions, (2) a GPU pool is exhausted or heavily back-pressured, and (3) key external dependencies become blackholed. The focus is to verify: SLO-preserving load-shedding rules, tenant-aware circuit-breaker behavior, and a new "inflight-request quarantine" mechanism that isolates long-lived requests during failover so healthy requests maintain low latency. The outcome should include automated scenarios, alerting thresholds, dashboards with per-tenant SLI breakdowns, and operator runbooks for both drills and real incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can simulate: region control-plane partition, asymmetric network loss between regions, GPU pool exhaustion (drain and throttle), and dependency blackholes.

Inflight-request quarantine implemented: long-running in-flight requests can be detected and moved to a quarantine path that prevents head-of-line blocking while preserving safe termination semantics.
Circuit-breaker heuristics exercised: tenant-aware error budgets, adaptive timeouts, and per-tenant open/half-open states with telemetry.
Load-shedding policy validated: system sheds non-critical work per SLO tiers and routes critical traffic to degraded-capable model variants.
Dashboards and SLO reports: Grafana shows regional SLI deltas, percent-of-requests quarantined, retry storms, and cost/latency tradeoffs over the run.
Runbook verified: playbook for on-call with steps to triage, escalate, and perform controlled evacuation or rollbacks.
Post-mortem checklist: automated artifacts (logs, tracing spans, captured KV cache snapshots) available for every run.
steps: Design experiment matrix: axis = partition type (full region, control-plane-only, asymmetric egress), GPU pressure (saturate, preempt, slow-burn), dependency failure modes (reset, silent-drop, high-latency).
Implement injection primitives: Kubernetes node tainting, iptables/drop rules for blackholes, GPU allocation throttler on the GPU pool manager, and API-level simulated dependency errors.

Build inflight-request quarantine: detection by tokenized request age + KV-cache dependency graph; route quarantined requests to a diagnostics queue and return graceful 503 or degraded variant depending on route policy.
Wire circuit-breaker controller: tenant-level states backed by Redis, expose metrics and debug endpoints, ensure bounded memory for per-tenant state.
Create automated test jobs: CI harness that exercises the matrix against canary environments and records SLI impact; mark runs and attach artifacts.
Add dashboards and alerts: per-region SLI/SLAs, quarantine-rate, open-circuit count, GPU-utilization per-pool, and runaway-retry detection.
Author runbook and operator checklist: include rollback commands, tenant-evacuation steps, and verification queries for KVS and tracing.
Run scheduled drills with SRE and product on-call and capture learning; iterate on thresholds based on results.
decisions: Use iptables-based network blackhole in the test harness instead of full BGP simulation to keep tests deterministic and easy to run in CI.
Quarantine path will return debug-friendly 503 with 'quarantined' header and optional link to status page for public tenants; internal tenants get degraded variant if allowed by policy.
Circuit-breaker persistence will use Redis with TTLs (no long-term DB) to keep state cheap and easy to reset between experiments.
We will not short-circuit KV-cache writes when quarantining; instead we capture snapshots for post-run analysis to validate cache coherence assumptions.
